name: Self-Referencing Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor

R337_result.root_cause: Biofouling (3 μV/day, only affects Element A) and creep (0.5 μV/day, asymmetric) are NOT common-mode. The dual-element approach cancels 67.8% of drift but the remaining 32.2% (biofouling + creep + mismatch) still produces 3.45 mmHg error over 30 days — above the 2.0 mmHg clinical threshold.
R337_result.interpretation: The self-referencing approach is PHYSICALLY SOUND (cancels common-mode drift) but INSUFFICIENT in practice (non-common-mode drift from biofouling dominates). The sensor needs additional anti-fouling measures or a different drift compensation strategy.

decision: T1 — computationally supported (model ran, physics is real) but FALSIFICATION FAILS. The model itself is valid; the MECHANISM is insufficient for the clinical threshold. This is a MECHANISM LIMITATION, not an implementation bug (Article XXIX).
repair_path: The candidate is NOT killed. It survives as T1 with a known limitation. The mechanism (differential sensing) is sound but needs enhancement: (1) anti-fouling coating on Element A, (2) periodic recalibration protocol, or (3) accept higher threshold (3.45 mmHg may be acceptable for trending, not absolute measurement). The buyer package must disclose this limitation honestly.

buyer_package_update.evidence_now: T1 — computational model shows 67.8% drift cancellation but remaining 3.45 mmHg error exceeds 2.0 mmHg clinical threshold. Mechanism is sound but insufficient alone for absolute pressure measurement. May be acceptable for trending.
known_failures: Falsification threshold (2.0 mmHg) NOT met — dual-element error 3.45 mmHg over 30 days
buyer_package_update.remaining_uncertainty: Whether anti-fouling coating or periodic recalibration can bring error below 2.0 mmHg
